name: Danny Harris
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Danny Harris owns popular athleisure brand Alo Yoga with his childhood friend turned business partner, Marco DeGeorge.
The pair met while growing up in the San Francisco suburb of Los Gatos and began selling T-Shirts together after graduating high school.
In 1992, Harris and DeGeorge launched Color Image Apparel and found success screen printing apparel for wholesale.
They created the Alo Yoga brand in 2007, and nearly two decades later, its $118 leggings and $68 biker shorts have become a hit with celebrities and influencers.
Alo Yoga made up the vast majority of Color Image Apparel's nearly $2 billion of estimated revenue in 2024.
Alo has expanded to more than 150 brick-and-mortar stores worldwide, including 56 outside the U.S.

name: Luo Yuhao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2022-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2023-2026); Hurun China U40 (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Luo Yuhao is vice president of Shanghai-based online games developer miHoYo.
He cofounded miHoYo in 2012 with college friends, Cai Haoyu and Liu Wei.
The company is best known for its anime-styled adventure games such as Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail.
Cai and Liu are also billionaires.
Apple CEO Tim Cook described that he found a "phenomenal team" at company after a visit to its headquarters in 2023.

name: Sergei Galitsky
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2020)
forbes_bio: Sergei Galitsky is the founder of Magnit, one of Russia's biggest supermarket chains and cosmetics retailers with more than 30,000 stores in 2024.
Galitsky was CEO of Magnit until February 2018 when he sold almost all of his shares in the company to the state bank VTB for $2.4 billion.
Galitsky got his start in 1994 as a perfume and beauty supplies wholesaler.
An admirer of Wal-Mart, he opened his first grocery store in 1998 and advertised using the slogan "Always Low Prices."
He took the company public in 2006.
forbes_facts: Galitsky owns the soccer team Krasnodar and a soccer academy. He has invested about $460 million in a new soccer stadium nicknamed Galiseum by local journalists.
Galitsky spent $70 million on a park near his soccer stadium, planting 2,500 trees.
With his brother-in-law, Galitsky owns a 173-acre winery that will soon be selling wine under the Galitsky & Galitsky label.

name: Farhad Moshiri
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2016)
forbes_bio: Farhad Moshiri is a business partner of Russian billionaire Usmanov, whom he met in the early 1990s.
An accountant by training, Moshiri once worked for such firms as Ernst & Young and Deloitte Touche.
Alongside Usmanov, he has stakes in Russian mining and steel manufacturing giant Metalloinvest and Russian wireless operator Megafon.

He sold a stake in London's Arsenal soccer club back to Usmanov in 2016 to fund his investment in another English club, Everton, selling the team to billionaire Dan Friedken in 2024 for about $625 million.
forbes_facts: Moshiri was born in Iran, but his parents left Iran just before the 1979 revolution.

name: Kabir Mulchandani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Kabir Mulchandani is the owner of Dubai-based real estate firm FIVE Holdings, which owns and operates luxury party hotels and resorts in the Middle East, New York, Spain and Switzerland.
He founded the firm in 2011 as SKAI Holdings and rebranded it as FIVE in 2017 as the group expanded into hospitality and lifestyle properties.
Born and raised in Mumbai, India, Mulchandani worked for his family's consumer electronics business before moving to Dubai in the early 2000s and investing in real estate.
After Dubai's property market collapsed in 2008, Mulchandani was charged with fraud and embezzlement in 2009 and spent 140 days in jail before being cleared in 2010.
FIVE Holdings acquired Pacha Group, which owns hotels and nightclubs in Ibiza, Spain, for $330 million in November 2023.

name: Randal J. Kirk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Randal Kirk, a former practicing attorney, is executive chairman of investment firm Third Security. Though the firm liquidated its life sciences-focused VC funds in 2020, it continues to manage Kirk's family money.
In 2020, he stepped down as CEO of biotech firm Precigen, but was appointed executive chairman.
He achieved his first entrepreneurial success with an injectable drug and vaccine distributor, which he eventually sold for $145 million.
His investments have made waves for innovative products, like apples that never brown and a genetically modified species of salmon.
Kirk sold greeting cards door-to-door when he was 9 years old, and claims he had an 85% close rate.
forbes_facts: Kirk's father was a master sergeant in the U.S. Air Force.
Kirk previously lived on a farm in Virginia, where he was an avid falconer.

name: Nicholas Howley
sec_insider_companies: TransDigm Group INC (TDG) - Director; Perimeter Solutions, Inc. (PRM) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: W. Nicholas Howley cofounded TransDigm through a 1993 leveraged buyout in which he acquired four struggling aerospace units from his employer, IMO Industries. He is currently its chairman.
The Cleveland-based aerospace parts manufacturer has grown into an $8.8 billion (sales) company through acquisitions of small companies that are the sole makers of particular components.
Howley has twice been called to testify before Congress over allegations the company has overcharged the Pentagon for spare parts.
He is also chairman of Perimeter Solutions, a chemical manufacturing company.
His family foundation has provided scholarships to hundreds of low-income students, primarily to attend Catholic high schools in Cleveland and Philadelphia.
